&l;p&g;Based on analysis of Santander Consumer USA Holdings&a;rsquo; (SC) 2017 10-K, I have downgraded the stock from neutral to unattractive. Analyst Eric Roll identified three significant red flags buried in the footnotes. 
On &l;a href=&q;https://www.newconstructs.com/wp-content/uploads/2018/03/SC_Tax_Benefit.png&q; target=&q;_blank&q; rel=&q;noopener noreferrer&q; target=&q;_blank&q;&g;page 119&l;/a&g;, SC reported a $678 million tax benefit (57% of GAAP net income) due to the revaluation of its deferred tax liabilities as a &l;a href=&q;https://www.newconstructs.com/tax-reform-winners-companies-with-deferred-tax-liabilities/&q; target=&q;_blank&q; rel=&q;noopener noreferrer&q; target=&q;_blank&q;&g;result of tax reform&l;/a&g;. This non-cash, one-time benefit allowed SC to report an effective tax rate of -44%. I adjusted for this non-operating item to keep SC&a;rsquo;s tax rate at its average of ~35%. 
On &l;a href=&q;https://www.newconstructs.com/wp-content/uploads/2018/03/SC_Change_In_Reserves.png&q; target=&q;_blank&q; rel=&q;noopener noreferrer&q; target=&q;_blank&q;&g;page 100&l;/a&g;, the company disclosed a $148 million decrease to its credit loss allowance (12% of GAAP net income). This &l;a href=&q;https://www.newconstructs.com/change-in-total-reserves/&q; target=&q;_blank&q; rel=&q;noopener noreferrer&q; target=&q;_blank&q;&g;decrease in reserves&l;/a&g; artificially inflated SC&a;rsquo;s reported net income in 2017. 
Finally, on &l;a href=&q;https://www.newconstructs.com/wp-content/uploads/2018/03/SC_Internal_Control.png&q; target=&q;_blank&q; rel=&q;noopener noreferrer&q; target=&q;_blank&q;&g;page 79&l;/a&g;, SC&a;rsquo;s auditor, Pricewaterhouse Coopers, stated its opinion that SC &a;ldquo;did not maintain, in all material respects, effective internal control over financial reporting.&a;rdquo; Specifically, PwC raised concerns over the models SC used to estimate its credit loss allowance. 
Any material weakness in internal controls should be a red flag for investors as these weaknesses are correlated with &l;a href=&q;http://journals.sagepub.com/doi/abs/10.1177/0148558X17696761&q; target=&q;_blank&q; rel=&q;noopener noreferrer&q; target=&q;_blank&q;&g;an increased risk of a stock price crash&l;/a&g;. In SC&a;rsquo;s case, the red flag is even larger due to the fact that its material weakness is related to the change in its credit loss allowance that artificially boosted net income by $148 million. 
In total, I made the following adjustments to Santander Consumer USA Holdings&a;rsquo; 2017 10-K: 
Income Statement: I made $805 million of adjustments, with a net effect of removing $796 million in non-operating income (12% of revenue). You can see all the adjustments made to SC&a;rsquo;s income statement &l;a href=&q;https://www.newconstructs.com/wp-content/uploads/2018/03/SC_IS_Adjustments.png&q; target=&q;_blank&q; rel=&q;noopener noreferrer&q; target=&q;_blank&q;&g;here&l;/a&g;. 
Balance Sheet: I made $3.4 billion of adjustments to calculate invested capital with a net increase of $3.3 billion (43% of reported net assets). Aside from the credit loss allowance referenced above, the largest adjustment was to add back $86 million in &l;a href=&q;https://www.newconstructs.com/off-balance-sheet-debt/&q; target=&q;_blank&q; rel=&q;noopener noreferrer&q; target=&q;_blank&q;&g;off-balance sheet debt&l;/a&g;. You can see all the adjustments made to DFS&a;rsquo;s balance sheet &l;a href=&q;https://www.newconstructs.com/wp-content/uploads/2018/03/SC_BS_Adjustments.png&q; target=&q;_blank&q; rel=&q;noopener noreferrer&q; target=&q;_blank&q;&g;here&l;/a&g;. 
&l;!–nextpage–&g; Valuation: I made $988 million of adjustments with a net effect of decreasing shareholder value by $988 million. The largest adjustment to shareholder value was $897 million in deferred tax liabilities. This adjustment represents 15% SC&a;rsquo;s market cap. 
After making all these adjustments, I found that SC&a;rsquo;s return on invested capital (&l;a href=&q;https://www.newconstructs.com/education-return-on-invested-capital/&q; target=&q;_blank&q; rel=&q;noopener noreferrer&q; target=&q;_blank&q;&g;ROIC&l;/a&g;) decreased from 10% to 4% in 2017, even as its GAAP net income increased by 55%. These misleading earnings make SC a high-risk stock for investors.
